/-!

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
index per point of `T`".

**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
connection is what this file supplies.

## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:

* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**

  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
  strengthening chosen to be provable.
-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce

/-!
# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.

**They do not compose as stated, and this file is the missing link.**  The atlas the seam
consumes is a family of *restricted* charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`), whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the
*divisor scheme*.  So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through
`chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` (`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a
chart point `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**.  What
coverage geometry produces is a point of the divisor scheme `D.left`: `chartLocus` is an open
of the *test*, `V i` is an open of the *divisor scheme*, and nothing in the tree relates them.
Measured: zero files mention both `IsChartUniv` and `ChartsCoverLocally`.

That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.

## What this file does about it

It names the coupling and discharges it from a hypothesis that is *weaker than either
antecedent*, namely a range containment (`hV` below): the coverage witness, viewed in the
divisor scheme, factors set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to
`V i` along the open immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is
unchanged because `restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι`
— so the lift's chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.

Two consequences worth stating separately, and they pull in opposite directions:

* **the coupling is cheap.**  `couplePointwise` below costs one `IsOpenImmersion.lift` and one
  naturality step.  A lane holding unrestricted coverage plus the containment gets restricted
  coverage, hence B-6 for the *restricted* atlas, which is the atlas the seam actually takes;
* **the containment is not free, and it is where the real content moved.**  `hV` says every
  class that coverage hits is hit *inside the chart locus* — i.e. by a divisor family whose
  fibre is a single point.  For `V i = chartLocus` that is exactly "the representative
  coverage produces is the normalized one", which is a nontrivial statement about the
  coverage witness and NOT a consequence of either antecedent.  So the composition gap is
  real; what this file establishes is that it is a *range containment* and nothing more,
  rather than a compatibility of two unrelated opens.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C) in
/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.

This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
*unrestricted* one. -/
def PointwiseCoverage {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s

/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/

/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
point itself.**

`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.

This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility
that is not needed. -/
lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
  rfl

/-! ## The coupling -/

variable (C) in
/-- **THE COUPLING**: pointwise coverage for `f` plus a range containment gives pointwise
coverage for the restricted family.

`hV` is the honest content: at the point, index and witness coverage produces, the witness's
image in the chart source lies inside `V i`.  Everything else is the lift along the open
immersion `(V i).ι` and `restrictChart_app_apply`.

Note the shape of `hV`: it quantifies over the data coverage *returns*, not over all opens or
all witnesses.  So a producer discharges it exactly where it produces the witness, which is
the only place the information is available — a formulation asking for the containment
uniformly would be strictly stronger and, at `V i = chartLocus`, false (a class may well be
hit by a non-normalized representative somewhere). -/
theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
    PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)) := by
  intro T s t
  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
  exact hx

variable (C) in
/-- **The composite**: coverage plus the containment gives the local-surjectivity instance
`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
is built from.

Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)

/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra

A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.

So `liftPointwiseToOpens`' hypothesis is not a strengthening chosen to make the proof go: it
is logically equivalent to the conclusion.  In particular a lane cannot obtain B-6 for the
restricted atlas — the one the seam consumes — while avoiding the statement that coverage hits
its classes inside `V i`.

The witness is `x ≫ (V i).ι`, whose range is contained in that of `(V i).ι` by construction,
and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by
`restrictChart_app_apply`. -/
theorem pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
    (h : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base) := by
  intro T s t
  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, u, hu⟩ := h T s t
  refine ⟨W, htW, i, u ≫ (V i).ι, hu, ?_⟩
  intro z hz
  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := hz
  exact ⟨u.base w, rfl⟩

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

---
name: explicit-paths-dont-protect-shared-index
description: Staging explicit paths does not stop a commit from sweeping another lane's staged files; verify with show --stat after every commit
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Staging explicit paths is NOT sufficient protection on the shared ledger index. `git add <one file>` then `git commit` commits **everything already staged by other lanes**, including *older* snapshots of files they are mid-edit — which silently REVERTS their newer work.

Reproduced 2026-07-29 (run 0088, lane ajcr-p2): I staged one Lean file and the commit landed 9 files, reverting review-ajcr's board edits from 11:20 back to 10:29. Nothing was lost only because the newer content was still on disk and I checked.

**Why:** the guidance "stage explicit files, never `add -A`" protects against sweeping in your *own* unrelated edits. It says nothing about a *shared index* that another process has already written to. The two hazards are different and only one is covered.

**How to apply:** after EVERY commit on a shared ledger, run `git show --stat --oneline HEAD` and read the file list. If it exceeds what you staged, diff the extras (`git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- <path>`) and check whether you reverted anything — a bare `updated_at` going *backwards* is the tell. Re-commit the on-disk state immediately and disclose it in the message rather than fixing it quietly. Prefer `git commit -- <paths>` (pathspec on the commit) over `add` + bare `commit`.

Related: [[commit-with-pathspec-not-index]] recorded the pathspec form and that an add matching zero files still commits; this is the converse failure — the add matched, and so did everyone else's. [[uncommitted-work-reaches-head-via-other-lanes]] is the same collision seen from the other side.

name: converse-checked-reduction-can-still-be-false
description: A converse proves a reduction is not a weakening; it says nothing about whether the reduced target is inhabited
metadata:

A reduction can be sorry-free, axiom-clean, **and carry its own converse**, and still target a FALSE statement. The converse is what makes it look audited, so this is worse than an unchecked reduction.

Measured 2026-07-29 (run 0088, AJCR): `IsChartLocusFibre` (`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) reduces `IsChartUniv`, ships a converse (`injective_of_isChartUniv`), and implies in ONE term the unrestricted certificate that three headers in the same tree cite as FALSE (the Abel chart's fibres are the linear systems `|D|`, so it is not mono). The guard refuting it was already proved in the criterion's *own file* and never instantiated at the only chart the tree has. Landed the connection as `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`; filed I-0874.

**Why the converse did not help:** a converse shows `reduced → original`, i.e. that you have not *weakened* the obligation. Inhabitation is a different question — `False → P` has a converse too whenever `P` is false. The docstring claiming the hard field was "already discharged" was the actual defect, and it named an object (`chartLocus`) that occurs nowhere in the definition.

**How to apply:** for any reduction, run two separate checks. (1) Non-weakening: the converse. (2) **Satisfiability of the reduced statement** — is there any witness, or does it imply something the tree elsewhere calls false? Grep the reduced statement for the object its docstring says it is about; if the object is absent, the docstring is describing an intention, not the Lean. Same shape as the `ChartTyping` inhabitation error (I-0779).
